Definition: from the base of G5007 and a derivative of the base of G3984; enduring trial, i.e. miserable:--wretched.
BiblicalUsage: Paul cries, O wretched man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death? And the risen Christ tells Laodicea that it calls itself rich while it is wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked. The word is enduring trial, miserable: the state of a person who has found out how bad things are.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's cry and Laodicea's blindness are the two sides of one truth: knowing you are wretched is the beginning of deliverance, and not knowing it is the danger.
